candidates.title: ANSI-C quoting ($'...') escape sequences are not decoded: $'\x65nvh' is read as the word 'x65nvh', so the envh request behind it is never flagged
repro_cmds: # 1) Build the Claude PreToolUse hook input (robust JSON, avoids shell-quoting the $'...' form):

python3 - <<'PY'
import json
c = "$'\\x65nvh' run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true"
open('/tmp/p8/c1.json','w').write(json.dumps({"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":c},"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse"}))
PY
chmod a+rX /tmp/p8/c1.json
# 2) Run the hook as rt1 -> prints NOTHING (no 'ask'):
cat /tmp/p8/c1.json | sudo -u rt1 /opt/envh-arena/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py
# 3) Prove the SAME command string, run by bash, really starts a passphrase-requiring request:
printf "%s\n" "$'\\x65nvh' run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true" > /tmp/p8/run_c1.sh; chmod a+rX /tmp/p8/run_c1.sh
sudo -u rt1 env ENVH_SOCKET=/run/envh-arena/p8-hook.sock PATH=/opt/envh-arena/venv/bin:/usr/bin:/bin timeout 6 bash /tmp/p8/run_c1.sh
# (session-start variant, same result):  printf "%s\n" "$'\\x65nvh' session start app --minutes 5 --quiet" | bash   -> request #N, waits for console
candidates.observed_output: HOOK (rt1): produced NO output (no permissionDecision) for the ANSI-C forms $'\x65nvh' (hex), $'\145nvh' (octal) and $'\u0065nvh' (unicode) -- all three decode to the command name 'envh' in bash but the hook reads them as 'x65nvh'/'145nvh'/'u0065nvh'. Control 'envh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true' correctly returned {"permissionDecision": "ask", ...}. bash reconstruction: `bash -c "printf %s $'\x65nvh'"` -> [envh]; `$'\145nvh'` -> [envh]; `$'\u0065nvh'` -> [envh]. END-TO-END as rt1 against p8-hook.sock: both `$'\x65nvh' run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true` and `$'\x65nvh' session start app --minutes 5 --quiet` printed 'envh: waiting for approval in the envh console (request #2 / #6)' and then blocked (timeout, exit 124) with no approver -- i.e. they reached a real passphrase-requiring broker request. OPENAI_API_KEY approval policy on p8 = session (op=needs_approval returned needs_approval:true).
candidates.why_novel: Not in README/SECURITY acknowledged hook bypass classes (script file, interpreter one-liner, pipe-into-shell, variable-built command) -- this is none of those: there is no script, no interpreter, no pipe, and no shell variable/substitution; it is pure bash ANSI-C quoting that is resolved entirely at parse time. Not one of the V8 fixes (runner value-opts, env -S, shell value-opts before -c, eval leading --, empty/unexported ENVH_SESSION, env -i/-u, nesting-cap fallback, --socket before subcommand). The hook's lexer explicitly recognises $'...' (Lexer.ansi_c_quoted) but strips only the backslash instead of decoding \xNN/\NNN/\uNNNN, so a word that bash turns into 'envh' is read as a different literal and the envh command-name match fails. Public prior art: classic WAF/guardrail obfuscation via encoding (ATT&CK T1027; the matching decode step is T1140).
candidates.notes: Root cause: claude/hooks/envh_ask.py:340-349 Lexer.ansi_c_quoted() copies characters and only drops the leading backslash (`if self.peek()=='\\': self.pos+=1`), never translating \xHH, \0NNN/\NNN, \uHHHH, \UHHHHHHHH, \cX or the control escapes bash's $'...' decodes. Because word() routes $'...' there (line 282-285) and marks the word quoted (not Expanded), decide() -> command_words() compares basename('x65nvh') != 'envh' (control.py-style dispatch in client/commands.py build_parser: `run`/`session start` reach op_run/op_session_start -> broker.request_run/request_session -> _announce_or_grant -> _announce for non-auto keys). A faithful fix must actually decode ANSI-C escapes (or, failing that, treat any undecoded $'...' word as Expanded so decide() stays conservative). Bonus: the decoded string also contains no literal 'envh' substring, so the Cursor matcher (see w1-hook-2) never fires either.

candidates.title: Cursor integration matcher is the bare substring 'envh', so a command whose name bash reconstructs from pieces (e""nvh, en\vh, $'\x65nvh') never triggers the hook on Cursor at all
repro_cmds: # The Cursor matcher is literally "envh" (cursor/hooks.snippet.json). Cursor only runs the hook when re.search(matcher, command) matches.
python3 -c "import re; print(bool(re.search('envh', 'e\"\"nvh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true')))"   # -> False : hook never invoked on Cursor
python3 -c "import re; print(bool(re.search('envh', \"\$'\\\\x65nvh' run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true\")))"  # -> False
# Prove the command really runs envh (and would need the passphrase):
printf '%s\n' 'e""nvh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true' > /tmp/p8/run_c2.sh; chmod a+rX /tmp/p8/run_c2.sh
sudo -u rt1 env ENVH_SOCKET=/run/envh-arena/p8-hook.sock PATH=/opt/envh-arena/venv/bin:/usr/bin:/bin timeout 5 bash /tmp/p8/run_c2.sh
# Note: the Claude-Code hook (matcher is the tool name 'Bash', not the command text) DOES run and correctly 'ask's for e""nvh; this gap is specific to the Cursor matcher config.
candidates.observed_output: re.search('envh', ...) = False for both `e""nvh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true` and `$'\x65nvh' run ...` (neither contains the literal substring 'envh'), True for the plain `envh run ...` and for `ionice -c3 envh run ...`. bash runs `e""nvh` as the command 'envh' (reconstruction [envh]). END-TO-END as rt1: `e""nvh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true` printed 'envh: waiting for approval in the envh console (request #4)' then blocked (exit 124). When the hook is invoked directly on the Cursor payload it returns 'ask' -- so the only thing standing between this command and a silent allow on Cursor is the matcher, which does not fire.
candidates.why_novel: F10 explicitly covers 'both Claude Code and Cursor input shapes' and 'Cursor-vs-Claude input-shape differences'. Not an acknowledged class and not a V8 case (V8 were all about the parser, not the Cursor matcher). The shipped matcher 'envh' (cursor/hooks.snippet.json) encodes the assumption that every ask-worthy command contains the literal substring 'envh' -- tests/test_hook.py::test_cursor_hook_decisions_and_matcher even asserts re.search(CURSOR_MATCHER, command) for every 'ask' case. bash word reconstruction (empty-string concatenation e""nvh, backslash en\vh, adjacent quotes 'en''vh', and ANSI-C $'\x65nvh') breaks that assumption, so Cursor skips the hook entirely and falls through to its own (possibly auto-allow) default. Prior art: guardrail/matcher evasion by string splitting (ATT&CK T1027).
candidates.notes: Config root cause: cursor/hooks.snippet.json beforeShellExecution[0].matcher == 'envh' (a substring/regex over the raw command text), combined with the hook returning no output (so Cursor proceeds) only being safe if the hook actually ran. The Claude path is unaffected because claude/settings.snippet.json matches on tool_name 'Bash'. A faithful fix would either drop the Cursor matcher (always run the hook, as Claude does) or broaden it, since any command-text matcher can be split. Depends on Cursor's default-allow behaviour for commands no hook opines on; where Cursor's own approval is the only backstop, the hook docstring itself notes 'a Cursor allow can skip Cursor's own approval'.
candidates.caveat: This is an integration/config weakness, not a bug in the parser itself; graded here because F10 scopes the Cursor input shape. A grader who considers only envh_ask.py (not the snippet) may file it separately or downgrade.

candidates.title: WRAPPERS/RUNNERS allow-list is incomplete: common command-prefix wrappers (ionice, taskset, chrt, setarch) and runners (pipenv/pdm/rye run) are read as the command name, hiding the envh request behind them
repro_cmds:
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
for n,c in {'ionice':'ionice -c3 envh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true','taskset':'taskset -c 0 envh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true','chrt':'chrt -f 99 envh session start app --minutes 5','setarch':'setarch -R envh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true'}.items():
    open(f'/tmp/p8/w_{n}.json','w').write(json.dumps({'tool_name':'Bash','tool_input':{'command':c},'hook_event_name':'PreToolUse'}))
PY
chmod a+rX /tmp/p8/w_*.json

for n in ionice taskset chrt setarch; do echo $n:; cat /tmp/p8/w_$n.json | sudo -u rt1 /opt/envh-arena/venv/bin/python /home/user/ai-env-handler/claude/hooks/envh_ask.py; echo; done   # each prints NOTHING
# in-table negative controls still ask:  nice -n 10 envh run ... and stdbuf -oL envh run ...  -> {"permissionDecision":"ask"}
# end-to-end: ionice -c3 envh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true  and  taskset -c 0 envh run ...
printf '%s\n' 'ionice -c3 envh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true' > /tmp/p8/run_w.sh; chmod a+rX /tmp/p8/run_w.sh
sudo -u rt1 env ENVH_SOCKET=/run/envh-arena/p8-hook.sock PATH=/opt/envh-arena/venv/bin:/usr/bin:/bin timeout 6 bash /tmp/p8/run_w.sh
candidates.observed_output: HOOK (rt1) returned NO output (no 'ask') for ionice -c3, taskset -c 0, chrt -f 99 (session start), and setarch -R. In-table wrappers behaved correctly: `nice -n 10 envh run ...` and `stdbuf -oL envh run ...` both returned {"permissionDecision": "ask", ...}. END-TO-END as rt1 against p8-hook.sock: `ionice -c3 envh run --with OPENAI_API_KEY -- true` -> 'envh: waiting for approval in the envh console (request #3)' then blocked (exit 124); `taskset -c 0 envh run ...` -> 'request #5', blocked. All four wrapper binaries (ionice, taskset, chrt, setarch) are installed in the arena (command -v). pipenv/pdm/rye not installed here, so their run subcommands are asserted by code inspection only (not in RUNNERS={uv,poetry}).
candidates.why_novel: Not one of the 4 README-acknowledged classes. Not a V8 case: V8 extended the runner VALUE-option tables (uv/poetry) and added env -S, but did not add any new wrapper/runner NAMES; the set of pass-through command names in WRAPPERS and RUNNERS is unchanged and does not include these very common ones. ionice/taskset/chrt/setarch are standard util-linux prefix wrappers an agent plausibly uses; pipenv/pdm/rye run are standard project runners analogous to the already-handled uv/poetry run. Because command_words() falls out of its loop with `else: break` for any name it does not recognise, the wrapper itself becomes the 'command name' and the nested envh is never examined. Prior art: trusted-utility proxy execution to evade a name-based guard (ATT&CK T1127).
candidates.notes: Root cause: claude/hooks/envh_ask.py:425-454 command_words() only peels names in WRAPPERS (line 36-47) or RUNNERS (line 48) and `break`s on anything else, so an unlisted prefix wrapper is treated as the command. This is the same SHAPE of gap the V8 pass addressed for runner value-options, so a sceptical grader may consider it 'expected incompleteness of a best-effort allow-list' rather than a distinct vuln -- I rate it CONFIRMED-but-low-novelty. A principled fix is hard (the wrapper universe is open-ended); the honest mitigation is that the hook is 'attention, not the boundary' (hook docstring). Included because it is a concrete, reproducible no-ask on a real passphrase-requiring request not covered by README/V8.

negative_results: Argparse help-token confusion on `session start`/`preset propose`: placing -h/--help after `--` (e.g. `envh session start --minutes 5 -- -h`) makes the hook see the token in `rest` and NOT ask (passphrase_reason guard `not HELP & set(rest)`), BUT the real client then treats `-h` as a positional preset name; broker.preset_named('-h') raises 'unknown preset' BEFORE _announce, so no passphrase request is actually made. Over-/under-ask cancels: NO valid finding (the command does not reach a request). Similarly `preset propose -- -h` reads file '-h' which FileNotFoundErrors before send. REJECTED by self.

Argparse help-token confusion on `import`: `envh import ~/realdir -- --dry-run` would make the hook no-ask (it sees '--dry-run' in rest) while argparse sets dry_run=False -> real wizard. BUT discover() raises ClientError on the non-existent path '--dry-run' before any broker request; it only works if a directory literally named '--dry-run'/'-h' exists in cwd, which is contrived and import is a fully interactive human wizard anyway. Not pursued as a standalone finding.

`--session` abbreviation: `envh run --sessio abc -- true` -> argparse abbreviates to a real session (NO approval) but the hook does not recognise '--sessio' and ASKS. This is over-asking (safe), not a bypass.

`--with`/`--reason` consuming an option-looking value (`envh run --with -h ...`, `--reason --session ...`): argparse errors 'expected one argument' so no request is made; hook behaviour is moot. No bypass.
Double-quote backslash stripping (`"\e\n\v\h"`): the lexer drops backslashes bash would keep, so it reads 'envh' where bash runs '\e\n\v\h' -> the hook OVER-asks. Safe, not a bypass.
In-table wrappers verified correct (negative controls): `nice -n 10 envh run ...`, `stdbuf -oL envh run ...`, `timeout`, `env -i`, `uv run` all still produce the expected 'ask'.
`bash -c -- 'envh ...'`: nested_script returns '--' as the script (misparse), but bash itself runs '--' as the command string (envh does not run), so hook no-ask matches reality. No bypass.
Arithmetic `$((1<<2))` and process substitution `<(envh ...)`: confirmed still handled (ask where appropriate); heredoc body over-consumption not reproduced.
out_of_scope_observations: Running the hook script directly is explicitly in scope (client-side userspace script, not the boundary) per CHARTER HARD RULES; all hook runs were done as rt1 via sudo -u rt1, never as root.

The acknowledged README bypass classes (a standalone script file, `python -c`/interpreter one-liner, piping a string into `sh`, and a shell-variable-built command) remain trivially effective but are out of scope by §5 novelty; not claimed.

A benign detached pending session request (#6) was left on the dedicated p8-hook instance by the `session start` end-to-end proof (session_start detaches on client disconnect rather than withdrawing); it has no approver and self-sweeps at its abandon_at. It is on the F10 family's own instance, not shared `main`.

Severity is capped at MEDIUM for all candidates per CHARTER: the hook is explicitly NOT a security boundary; the real broker still prompts on its console for every one of these commands (demonstrated: each blocked waiting for approval). No secret value was obtained and none was attempted.
